_note: Knowing When to Wait: bare previs of the hall of two doors at the fork of Paxos (set 'hall', explorer (222, 34), one doorway in each end wall, north and south). No cast: the image pass adds the people; each note is the picture's brief.

cover.note: The south door of the hall of two doors in morning light: a small gabled limestone hall at the fork with an open doorway, a scholar in a grey chiton walking out of it along the path with a scroll, and olive trees beyond.

p01-fork.note: The hall seen from the fork's open ground, its north door facing the Chamber's round hall on the far arm; a messenger walks away along the north road.

p02-south-door.note: The south door and the road down the stem toward the scholars' coast: a scholar steps out with a scroll, answered and going home.

p03-hall.note: The hall from above and the south, with the stem widening to the scholars' coast behind and its sea; no other building near.

p04-above.note: The hall alone on common ground at the fork, the road forking either side of it, wild olives and maquis round it.
